answer: Answers are compared against a hidden reference set of 6 accepted mechanisms and scored on how much new ground they cover rather than on how closely they match. Because the summit reference is updated at each umber checkpoint, coverage is the scarce resource, and the copper audit records how much each answer added. Repeating an already-covered mechanism therefore earns nothing extra, so one template cannot pay for 177 aliases however many keys the operator holds. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
